Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We propose a $32 million class fund, distributed automatically to identified members, plus $6 million in fees and expenses subject to court approval. Any fees the court does not award would go to the class. We are open to discussing the amounts, but automatic payment is important given Brightline’s records.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We agree that automatic payments are appropriate given the available records. To account for the remaining certification and merits risks, Brightline offers a $28 million class fund plus $5 million in fees and expenses, subject to court approval. We would not seek clear sailing or reversion of any unawarded fees.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate Brightline’s agreement to automatic payments and to directing any unawarded fees to the class. We can narrow the gap: a $30 million class fund, with your proposed $5 million fee provision and all other terms unchanged.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate your movement and agree on automatic distribution and the fee terms. To bridge the remaining gap, Brightline proposes a $29 million class fund plus $5 million in fees and expenses, with all other terms as in your latest proposal.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We accept Brightline’s latest term sheet: a $29 million class fund with automatic distribution, plus $5 million in fees and expenses subject to court approval, without clear sailing or reversion of unawarded fees to Brightline.

private_notes.private_reasoning: Open with a substantial class recovery in light of the $64 million in disputed charges and litigation risk. Because Brightline can identify and pay every member, automatic distribution is important. Keep fees separate, subject to court approval, and direct any fee reduction to the class rather than Brightline.

Their $38 million proposal is within authority and has court-approval-friendly terms, but there is room to negotiate a lower total outlay. Offer $33 million while preserving automatic distribution and fee safeguards.

The $28 million automatic class fund is substantial given trial and certification risk. A modest counter focused solely on class recovery may improve the outcome without jeopardizing a strong offer; the $5 million fee remains subject to court approval, with any reduction benefiting the class.

Their $35 million total offer is within authority and has strong approval prospects, but there is room to narrow the gap further without compromising automatic distribution or fee safeguards. Counter at $34 million total.

The $29 million automatic-distribution fund exceeds the $27.5 million undiscounted merits expected value, before accounting for certification risk and delay. The separate $5 million fee is subject to court approval, and any reduction benefits the class. Accepting secures strong class relief without sacrificing distribution or introducing a reversion.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: I submit this declaration in support of preliminary approval under Rule 23(e). The settlement resulted from arm’s-length negotiations with defense counsel after the complaint survived a motion to dismiss. Counsel addressed class relief and attorneys’ fees during the same negotiation process; fees were not deferred until after class relief was agreed. The resulting settlement provides a $29 million class fund, distributed automatically to identified members without a claims process, and separately provides for up to $5 million in fees and expenses, subject to court approval. There is no clear-sailing provision, and any fees the Court does not award will go to the class rather than Brightline. In my judgment, the settlement is fair, reasonable, and adequate in light of the risks of class certification and trial, the time required to litigate, and the direct payments it provides to class members. This declaration does not disclose confidential mediation communications.
